top_signals.title: China Goes on Oil Buying Spree as Crude Prices Slide
top_signals.summary: Chinese refiners have started buying more crude oil from abroad, taking advantage of lower prices in recent weeks to replenish the country’s oil inventories, Bloomberg has reported, citing traders. According to the report, Sinopec has bought about 20 million barrels of crude since the start of this month from West Africa alone, for loading in December. This compares with 20-25 million barrels of West African crude for all Chinese buyers monthly, on average. Yet Chinese refiners are also stepping up their purchases of Middle Eastern and Brazilian…

top_signals.title: China Hits Back at New Trump Tariff Prospects
top_signals.summary:
China called the prospect of new US tariffs on its exports “political maneuvering” and said the two nations should work together to maintain their trade truce. 

Jensen Huang struck a somber tone a day after his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, apologizing to employees during an all-hands meeting and sharing that he’d been in daily therapy to address the behavior that led to his brief ouster from the top job.

A global selloff in technology stocks is showing no sign of letting up as questions about the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade pile up.

Today’s guests: Christian Mueller-Glissman, Goldman Sachs Head of Asset Allocation Research; Xiaolan Fu, Oxford University Technology & International Development Professor & Centre of Technology and Industrialisation for Development Founding Director; Caitlin Egen, Control Risks Digital Risks Director. (Source: Bloomberg)
